transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Peregrine), Samir Desai (Peregrine), Marta Lopez (Peregrine), Alex Chen (Peregrine)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): walked through Console toggles to disable request storage per route, demoed PII redaction via rule sets, discussed ephemeral request headers for no-logs mode, quick Optimize recommendations for quantization when working with PHI-esque datasets.

00:00:12 Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we'll keep this focused on the sensitive-data controls, redaction and the API flags that let you make requests ephemeral.
00:00:25 Dr. Elena Ruiz: thanks, Maya. high level — we have PHI patterns in some prompts and we're trying to minimize logs being stored in vendor systems, and also want deterministic retention windows.
00:00:40 Maya Patel: yep understood. jonah and priya will demo the Console and then we'll show the api headers. quick question before we jump in: what's your current logging pipeline for requests?
00:00:55 Samir Desai: we push everything to our splunk cluster, and we also retain raw request payloads for 90 days — that's corporate policy — but security is pushing to drop vendor retention for sensitive routes.
00:01:12 Jonah Kim: okay, makes sense. we'll show two knobs: per-route request-storage toggles in Console, and an API-level ephemeral header x-redwood-ephemeral that bypasses storage. note transcription may mangle some of our acronyms, sorry in advance.
00:01:30 Priya Anand: starting screen share — Console -> Projects -> Peregrine-poc -> Routes. show toggle: "Store requests" true/false. by default it's true for debugging; flip to false and that route will not store request/response bodies.
00:01:58 Marta Lopez: quick q — does that also remove derived embeddings and usage metrics or just the raw request body?
00:02:10 Priya Anand: good question. disabling storage removes request/response bodies from the persistent request-store but we still emit aggregate metrics (tokens, latencies) to the metrics plane for billing and SLOs. embeddings and vectors are treated as derived artifacts and there are separate controls to avoid storing embeddings — there's a "suppress embeddings" checkbox and also an Optimize-offload option.
00:02:40 Alex Chen: and what about logs that go into our observability — like traces, audit logs — do they stop?
00:02:51 Jonah Kim: audit logs remain — we keep control-plane metadata (user, route, timestamp) in the audit log for compliance. we avoid storing PII in audit logs; the audit record has pointers but not the full payload. we can show how we redact fields in audit entries.
00:03:10 Dr. Elena Ruiz: show the redaction rules — regex-based? can they handle names / MRNs / dates?
00:03:20 Priya Anand: yes they're rule-based; you can upload a set or use our managed PII rule pack. demo: Policies -> Redaction. open rule: "Default-PHI-Strip". we have prebuilt patterns for SSN, MRN, emails, phone numbers, and you can add custom regexes for your MRN format.
00:03:42 00:04:00 Jonah Kim: (notes) sometimes regexes are too brittle; we also support model-assisted redaction where a small model tags spans and then you map to a rule. be aware model-assisted redaction adds a small processing cost and latency.
00:04:20 Samir Desai: latency is a concern. our SLO for patient-facing flows is 300ms. how much headroom does model-assisted redaction take?
00:04:32 Jonah Kim: depends on sequence length. for short prompts we've seen +40-90ms. Optimize will suggest using prefix caching + inline redaction for common PHI fields to stay under SLO. you can also route these to Dedicated GPU pools if you want consistent latency.
00:04:55 Maya Patel: high level tradeoff is cost/latency/accuracy. if you want the strictest no-storage guarantees you can combine ephemeral header + redaction + disable embeddings.
00:05:12 Dr. Elena Ruiz: what about the API header? show the exact curl.
00:05:20 Jonah Kim: switching to terminal. sample: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'x-redwood-ephemeral: true' -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2", "input":"..." }' . when ephemeral is true we short-circuit persistence; no request or response bodies are written to the request-store.
00:05:55 Marta Lopez: is ephemeral honored across Dedicated and Private?
00:06:03 Jonah Kim: yes. for Dedicated it obeys the same runtime policy. for Private we support a "private no-store mode" where nothing leaves the customer boundary; audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudPub but with redaction options. caveat: if you enable third-party integrations that mirror data (e.g. analytics), those need separate config.
00:06:25 Alex Chen: KMS integration? we want envelope encryption for logs at rest.
00:06:32 Priya Anand: we have KMS/HSM integration; logs and request-store can be encrypted with customer-managed keys. show Settings -> Security -> KMS. you can set key rotation policies and see key id used for audit entries.
00:06:50 00:07:05 Dr. Elena Ruiz: ok good — regulatory question: retention windows, can we set sub-24-hour retention for a route?
00:07:15 Priya Anand: yes you can set retention in Console per route: 24h, 7d, 30d, custom in days. sub-24h currently not in UI, but you can set ephemeral header which gives immediate no-store semantics. we can file a feature request for 12h retention if that's a must.
00:07:40 Samir Desai: logs into splunk — can Redwood push event-only audit records excluding payloads?
00:07:49 Jonah Kim: yes, we have an events webhook that pushes structured audit events (route id, user id, token, timestamp) but not payload. you can filter fields further in the webhook.
00:08:05 Marta Lopez: about Optimize — can it recommend quantization so we trade model size for lower cost without sacrificing PHI masking?
00:08:16 Maya Patel: Optimize will analyze token distributions and suggest quantization or smaller model families for latency/cost curve. it also simulates quality regressions against your eval set; for PHI you should include redaction tests in the evals to ensure masking still works.
00:08:40 Dr. Elena Ruiz: will Optimize flag failed masking regressions automatically? we need alerts when redaction stops working after a model rollout.
00:08:52 Jonah Kim: yes, we support eval-based regression alerts — you upload prompt sets and expected redaction outputs; if quality dips we send regression alerts and can auto-rollback.
00:09:05 Alex Chen: show us a live example of a route with redaction on.
00:09:12 Priya Anand: back to Console — open test-run tool. input: "Patient John Doe MRN 123-45-678" -> run. console shows masked output: "Patient [REDACTED] MRN [REDACTED]". note: occasional false positives/negatives possible.
00:09:45 Samir Desai: in that demo the MRN matched a pattern. if we need more context-aware masking (e.g., redact only if it's in a PHI field), how to do that?
00:09:55 Jonah Kim: you can configure redaction to only run on specified JSON paths or request fields; for chat-like prompts you can set heuristics to only mask in user message fields. also we support fine-grained allow-lists for tokens that should never be redacted (e.g., internal product codes).
00:10:18 Maya Patel: interruption — does your compliance require data residency?
00:10:23 Dr. Elena Ruiz: yes EU residency for EU patients; most production to be in eu-west-1.
00:10:30 Priya Anand: we can pin routes to regions and Dedicated clusters; Private supports full on-prem. routing policy in Console -> Deployment -> Region pin.
00:10:45 00:11:05 Jonah Kim: perf note: routing to a region farther from users can add latency; for sensitive patient flows often we suggest Dedicated capacity in the same region.
00:11:20 Marta Lopez: cost question — if we use ephemeral header frequently, are we billed differently?
00:11:28 Maya Patel: ephemeral doesn't change token billing; it's about persistence. but some features like model-assisted redaction or additional evals will add compute charges. Optimize can model the cost impact and show per-route cost delta.
00:11:45 Samir Desai: are there enterprise controls for role-based access to toggle storage? we don't want devs accidentally disabling retention.
00:11:54 Priya Anand: yes RBAC — only admins or roles with policy can change route storage. we show Role Management -> policies: allow:toggle_store, allow:edit_redaction.
00:12:10 Alex Chen: what about downstream backups — does Redwood maintain any temporary caches that could be snapshots of payloads?
00:12:20 Jonah Kim: runtime KV caches exist for generation performance, but they are memory-resident and scrubbed on instance restart; they are not persisted to durable storage when ephemeral is set. we'll include architecture docs for the cache lifecycle in the follow-up.
00:12:42 00:13:00 Dr. Elena Ruiz: can we see how audit logs look?
00:13:05 Priya Anand: show audit viewer. audit rows: timestamp, route id, user id, operation, redaction_status, key_id. the "redaction_status" indicates whether redaction rules matched and how many fields were redacted.
00:13:25 Marta Lopez: is there a tamper-evident log option?
00:13:30 Jonah Kim: yes you can push signed audit events to your SIEM with a signature header. Private deployments can run a signed append-only log via the HSM integration.
00:13:45 00:14:05 Samir Desai: legal will want a paper trail for change of retention settings. can we export the change history?
00:14:12 Priya Anand: yes, every change to route settings has an audit entry with actor and timestamp, exportable as CSV.
00:14:25 Dr. Elena Ruiz: edge case: what if a user sends PHI in a free-text prompt that triggers a model API call to an external tool? do we detect and prevent tool calls that leak?
00:14:38 Jonah Kim: we support function/tool call controls where you can restrict or sanitize parameters passed to external tools. also you can set a denylist for outbound connectors on Private deployments.
00:14:58 Maya Patel: going to demo ephemeral vs stored side-by-side with two routes. route-a: stored on, route-b: stored off. I'll run identical prompt and show request-store.
00:15:10 00:15:30 Maya Patel: running test... route-a shows recent request body in request-store and raw text visible to compliance; route-b shows no body and only audit entry. you'll see request id but clicking returns 404 for the body.
00:15:52 Marta Lopez: perfect.
00:16:00 Samir Desai: ok a few implementation Qs: SDK support for ephemeral flag? webhooks for events? and are there code examples for java/.net?
00:16:12 Jonah Kim: SDKs support an ephemeral param in all official SDKs: python, node, java. webhooks for audit events exist; language examples in our docs repo. i'll attach code snippets after.
00:16:30 Priya Anand: note: some older SDK versions pre-1.5 may not include header helpers, so recommend upgrading.
00:16:45 00:17:05 Dr. Elena Ruiz: security question: if we disable embeddings storage, are embeddings still materialized ephemeral for a moment? any chance they are persisted in logs?
00:17:18 Jonah Kim: embeddings are generated and may exist in memory for the request; we don't persist them when suppress embeddings is enabled. we also redact embeddings from internal debug logs; debug logs are only enabled in troubleshooting sessions with explicit consent.
00:17:40 Alex Chen: compliance asks for proof that redaction works — can we run a benchmark?
00:17:48 Maya Patel: yes — recommended: prepare a representative prompt set with ground-truth PHI spans and we'll run a masking benchmark with false-positive/negative rates. we'll use that for a POI acceptance criteria.
00:18:05 Samir Desai: timeline for pilot? we'd like to start a small pilot next month and evaluate for 6 weeks.
00:18:12 Maya Patel: sounds good. next steps: we'll send a pilot runbook with suggested evals and the redaction checklist.
00:18:25 00:18:40 Jonah Kim: one more thing — cross-customer leak: we never index customer data for training unless you opt in; this is part of our data-use policy. i'll point you to the docs.
00:18:55 Dr. Elena Ruiz: ok, show pricing delta if we enable model-assisted redaction and dedicated region.
00:19:05 Maya Patel: quick ballpark: model-assisted redaction add ~15-30% compute on top of inference cost for short prompts; Dedicated has a monthly reserved cost plus lower per-token in heavy throughput. Jamie on Pricing will follow up with a tailored estimate.
00:19:30 00:19:50 Marta Lopez: action on our side: confirm region and pilot user list.
00:19:58 Samir Desai: we'll do that and share retention policy.
00:20:10 Maya Patel: ok wrapping up — recap of commitments: send redaction checklist, sample SDK/curl for ephemeral, pilot runbook and eval template, and high-level pricing.
00:20:25 Dr. Elena Ruiz: thanks — good session.
00:20:30 Maya Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the threads.

End notes: demo lasted roughly 43 minutes; there were a couple of short tangents on KMS and Dedicated routing. audio had minor transcription errors (names and K V cache sometimes misrendered). Attachments referenced: "redaction-checklist.pdf" (will be shared), "ephemeral-examples.zip" (SDK snippets), "pilot-runbook.md".
